title: backend: memory CRUD + FTS5 search + build_memory_block
description: Migration 0002_memory_fts: FTS5 virtual table memories_fts(value, tags_text, key) content=memories + insert/update/delete triggers. MemoryService: CRUD, search (bm25 + importance, pinned union), build_memory_block(agent, query, k). Endpoints GET/POST /api/agents/{id}/memories?q=&tags=, PATCH/DELETE /api/memories/{id}. Wire memory_store/memory_recall tools. Tests.
close_reason: Memory + FTS5 done: alembic 0002_memory_fts (standalone FTS5 memories_fts(memory_id UNINDEXED, value, tags_text, key) + after insert/update/delete triggers + backfill; downgrade drops triggers explicitly so downgrade-to-base then replay passes). Standalone rather than content=memories because memories.id is a uuid-hex text PK, not the integer rowid external-content FTS5 maps through. memory/service.py: CRUD, search (bm25 minus importance*0.5, since bm25 is lower-is-better, so a 5/5 fact outranks a marginally better textual match), pinned_memories, build_memory_block (pinned union matched, deduped, capped at 4000 chars, empty string when memory is off so the prompt builder drops the section), build_match_query (strips FTS5 syntax and rebuilds prefix terms joined by OR - without it a query like 'cost:  (net)' is an FTS syntax error reaching the agent as a 500). api/memory.py: GET/POST /api/agents/{id}/memories?q=&tags=, GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/memories/{id}. runtime/tools/memory_tools.py binds memory_store/memory_recall per run with their own short-lived sessions; both return prose observations, refuse an empty or oversized value with a reason the agent can act on, and fall back to kind=fact on an invented kind. Required an include_name filter in alembic/env.py (applied by the cleaner) - the FTS5 table and its five shadow tables exist in no model, so alembic check proposed dropping all six. 43 tests. make check_backend green, 401 passed.

title: backend: agent runtime turn (DSPy ReAct + streamify) with persistence and stop
description: Conversations/messages CRUD (GET/POST /api/conversations, GET …/messages?after_seq=). runtime/prompt_builder.py (profile + attribution instructions + memory block + policy summary; per-message instruction stays on user turn), history.py -> dspy.History, agent_runner.run_turn: LMFactory, ReAct('system_instructions, history: dspy.History, user_message -> answer', gated tools, max_iters) in dspy.streamify(stream_listeners=[StreamListener('answer')], status_message_provider=RuntimeStatusProvider(hub), async_streaming=True) under dspy.context(lm, track_usage=True); stream_adapter maps StreamResponse->message.delta, StatusMessage->run.status, Prediction->message.completed; persist assistant message, tool_calls, usage_records, agent_runs. RunRegistry: one run per conversation (409), stop() = task.cancel + upstream POST /exec/:id/cancel with messageId, partial text status=stopped, run.stopped. Global semaphore max_concurrent_runs. DummyLM tests. Verify dspy 3.3 API at install (async tools in ReAct.acall, streamify async gen, StatusMessageProvider hook names).
close_reason: Agent runtime turn done: services/conversation_service.py (conversations/messages CRUD, seq allocated in one place, recent_pairs, set_active_run, auto-title from the first user message), runtime/prompt_builder.py (profile + instructions + duties + memory block + tool policy; sections omitted rather than emitted empty; per-message instruction stays on the user turn so it applies once), runtime/history.py (dspy.History from complete user/assistant pairs, summary prepended as a synthetic exchange, a repeated user message supersedes), runtime/run_registry.py (one run per conversation, run_id-guarded release, global semaphore, tracked in-flight sandbox messageIds), runtime/stream_adapter.py (StreamResponse->message.delta, StatusMessage->run.status, Prediction->message.completed; matches real DSPy types via isinstance, not class names), runtime/tools/{sandbox_tools,user_tools}.py, runtime/agent_runner.py (start_turn writes user+streaming-assistant bubbles and the run row before the model is touched; ReAct+streamify under dspy.context(track_usage=True); succeeded/stopped/failed/no-model all settle the run row rather than raising; stop cancels the guest command through POST /exec/:id/cancel). TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED, both silent: (1) dspy.streamify defaults to is_async_program=False, which drives the program's SYNC __call__ - every async tool returned an un-awaited coroutine that ReAct recorded as the observation, so a turn completed having executed nothing, with only a RuntimeWarning in the logs. Fixed with is_async_program=True. (2) The gate's wrapper was async def gated(**kwargs), so inspect.signature reported no parameters and DSPy built an empty argument schema; fixed with functools.wraps(call) so __wrapped__ carries the implementation's real signature. Also: PolicyEvaluator now treats an unflushed agent's risk_profile=None as the declared default instead of raising KeyError(None), and a cancelled sandbox command stays tracked (untracking it in a finally left the stop path with nothing to cancel and the guest process running forever). DSPy 3.3.1 verified: async tools work inside ReAct.acall, dspy.context is contextvar-safe across concurrent asyncio tasks (3 interleaved tasks kept their own LM), streamify yields only a Prediction for a non-streaming LM. No asyncify fallback needed. 35 tests. make check_backend green, 436 passed, cov 94.6%.

close_reason: Chat REST + output-only WS shipped. title: backend: sandbox admin pass-through (optional)
description: GET /api/sandbox/templates, GET /api/sandbox/sessions (projected {id,state,createdAt,lastActivity,templateName} — never proxy GET /exec/ verbatim), GET/POST /api/sandbox/keys, POST …/{id}/revoke|rotate, DELETE …/{id}, GET /api/sandbox/metrics (Prometheus text pass-through), ready check includes sandbox /health.
close_reason: Sandbox admin pass-through done: api/sandbox_admin.py with GET /api/sandbox/templates|sessions|keys|metrics, POST /keys, POST /keys/{id}/rotate|revoke, DELETE /keys/{id}. All admin-cookie gated; sandbox Bearer key stays server-side. Sessions are re-serialised through SessionInfo, never proxied verbatim. Scopes validated against {exec,admin,metrics} before the upstream call. Upstream 401/403 maps to 502 (operator key misconfigured) rather than 401, so a sandbox failure does not look like the browser session expiring. Key create/rotate/revoke/delete audited; secret returned once, never stored. Client gained keys/create_key/rotate_key/revoke_key/delete_key/metrics; response handling extracted to sandbox/http.py and shared with session.py; sandbox/deps.py adds SandboxDep/SandboxWSDep. Fake sandbox app gained /admin/keys/* and /metrics plus an admin_status_override for error-path tests. Contract note: sandbox types switched from alias= to validation_alias= so upstream camelCase parses in but this API serialises snake_case (FastAPI serialises response models with by_alias=True, which would otherwise have leaked createdAt/lastActivity/templateName into our responses). Not done here: PLAN also wants GET /api/ready to include the sandbox /health probe - api/health.py is held by the cleaner, raised on the team thread. 17 tests; make check_backend green, 129 passed, cov 96.6%.

close_reason: LLM providers/models + LMFactory + usage done: utils/crypto.py (Fernet key derived from secret_key via HKDF with domain-separation info; documented and tested consequence that rotating secret_key makes stored keys undecryptable, with an error saying to re-enter them), services/llm_service.py (provider+model CRUD, resolve_key from ciphertext or api_key_env, to_read projecting has_key/key_last4 only - no route ever returns a key), schemas/llm.py, api/llm.py (GET/POST /api/llm/providers, PATCH/DELETE, POST /{id}/test, GET/POST /api/llm/models, PATCH/DELETE), runtime/lm_factory.py (LMConfig separates resolution from construction so the test endpoint can report the resolved model without building an LM; prefixes openai|anthropic|xai, openai_compatible maps to openai since the prefix names the protocol not the vendor; cache=False because a cached tool-using turn would replay a stale decision against a changed workspace; dspy imported lazily to keep LiteLLM out of unrelated tests), services/usage_service.py (cost priced per million from the model row at call time so a later price edit cannot rewrite history; extract_tokens sums every model in a prediction; empty usage means not-tracked and writes nothing rather than recording zero). Switching a provider to an env ref drops the stored ciphertext so no shadow credential remains. Provider test always returns 200 with a reason - a failing provider is a result the settings page renders, not a 5xx. DSPy 3.3.1 verified: dspy.LM passes api_key/api_base through to LiteLLM, ReAct.acall exists, streamify(program, status_message_provider, stream_listeners, include_final_prediction_in_output_stream, is_async_program, async_streaming=True default), StatusMessageProvider hooks are lm_start/lm_end/module_start/module_end/tool_start/tool_end_status_message. 56 tests. make check_backend green, 401 passed, cov 96.5%.

Contract decision: list endpoints answer {"agents": [...]} / {"attributions": [...]} rather than bare arrays, consistent with the sandbox admin routes, leaving room for pagination. title: start.sh: mount /proc, /sys, devtmpfs, devpts, /dev/shm in the guest
description:
`docker export` ships no device nodes and mounts nothing, so the guest boots with empty
/proc and /sys, and a /dev containing only `dev/console` (a zero-byte regular file) plus
empty `dev/pts/` and `dev/shm/` directories.

node and socat tolerate this. Chromium does not: it dies immediately with SIGTRAP
(`<process did exit: exitCode=null, signal=SIGTRAP>`, surfaced by Playwright as
"Target page, context or browser has been closed"). busybox `df` also fails with
"can't find mount point" because /proc/mounts is absent.

Fix in minimal-rootfs/start.sh, before the existing tmpfs mounts, each guarded with
`2>/dev/null || true` to match the file's style:

    mount -t proc proc /proc
    mount -t sysfs sysfs /sys
    mount -t devtmpfs devtmpfs /dev
    mkdir -p /dev/pts /dev/shm
    mount -t devpts devpts /dev/pts
    mount -t tmpfs -o size=256m,mode=1777 tmpfs /dev/shm

This is the shared base image, so every template must be rebuilt to pick it up.

Verified: after the change, guest `mount` reports devtmpfs on /dev, proc on /proc,
sysfs on /sys, devpts on /dev/pts and tmpfs on /dev/shm; /dev/null and /dev/urandom are
character devices; Chromium then launches, navigates and screenshots successfully
(1280x720 PNG from example.com).

Blocks the desktop template (g9h.3) — Xvnc and Chromium cannot run without this.
close_reason: Shipped in 7433590 (start.sh mounts proc/sys/devtmpfs/devpts/dev-shm); verified present in HEAD

title: init
build.sh: resolve node absolutely; sudo secure_path hides nvm/fnm/volta
description:
templates/build.sh calls `npx tsc -b` and `sudo node dist/create_snapshot.js`. Under sudo
PATH is replaced by secure_path, so a node installed under the user's home (nvm, fnm,
volta) is invisible. The build dies at step [4/4] with "npx: command not found" — after
the 2 GiB dd, mkfs and docker export have already run.

The inner `sudo` is also an env_reset, which drops the VM_* resource variables the
snapshot creation needs, so `sudo -E env VM_MEM_SIZE_MIB=... ./templates/build.sh` does
not reach create_snapshot.js.

Fix:
- root guard at the top so the script fails fast with the correct invocation
- resolve NODE_BIN from `command -v node`, then $SUDO_USER's nvm/fnm/volta directories,
  honouring an explicit NODE_BIN= override
- invoke node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc directly rather than the npx shim, whose
  `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang has the same PATH problem
- drop the inner sudo (redundant once the root guard exists, and removing it eliminates
  the env_reset rather than working around it with -E)
- chown dist/ back to $SUDO_UID so a later non-sudo `npm run build` still works

Verified on a host with node 26.7.0 under ~/.nvm.

title: vm-manager: apply per-template resource limits at snapshot restore
description:
create_snapshot.ts writes template.json with no `resources` object, and vm-manager.ts
merges only memSizeMib and vcpuCount from it — both of which Firecracker takes from the
snapshot state on /snapshot/load anyway, so the override is currently a no-op.

The limits that actually matter are the jailer cgroup arguments: memoryLimitBytes,
cpuQuotaUs, cpuPeriodUs, pidsLimit, noFileSoftLimit. Those come from loadResourceConfig()
read from the server's environment at startup. A template built with
VM_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES=2147483648 therefore restores under the server's global default
(134217728), and the host cgroup OOM-kills the VM as soon as the guest touches more than
128 MiB. Raising the value globally instead would loosen containment for every other
template on the host.

Fix:
- create_snapshot.ts persists the full VmResourceConfig into template.json `resources`
- templates.ts widens TemplateManifest.resources to all seven fields
- vm-manager.ts merges every field, validating each is a positive finite number

Verified: GET /exec/templates reports browser at memoryLimitBytes 1610612736 / vcpu 2 /
cpuQuotaUs 200000 while node keeps 134217728 / vcpu 1 / 50000.

Prerequisite for g9h.3: its build.env sizing has no runtime effect without this.
g9h.2 sources build.env at build time, which is a different problem — it does not make
the values apply at restore.
close_reason: Shipped in 1ab9c6b (create_snapshot persists full resources; vm-manager merges all seven with validation); verified present in HEAD

title: exec: write route pins the session to the default template
description:
The write route passed `undefined` as templateName to sendSessionMessage, and its body
accepted no `template` field. Whichever request provisions the VM fixes the session's
template, and ensureSession's fast path returns the existing VM while ignoring any
templateName passed later.

Writing a file and then executing with {"template":"browser"} therefore ran on a node VM
and failed with "Cannot find module 'playwright-core'" — with shot.js present, because
the write had landed in that same node VM. Confusing to diagnose.

Fix: accept and forward `template` on the write route, with the same validation the
execute route applies (string, <= 64 chars).

Also worth documenting in the REST API section: a session's template is fixed by the
first request that touches it, and `template` on a live session is ignored.

title: README: reconcile with base64 read, build.env, and boot hooks
description:
Three closed beads shipped code but left their README task undone. The result is
documentation that now contradicts the shipped behaviour. Closed beads are not being
reopened; this tracks the correction.

## 1. g9h.8 — read?encoding=base64 shipped, README still says the endpoint is text-only

The route, SDK (`sdk/typescript/src/session.ts:139`) and MCP (`src/mcp/server.ts:141`)
all support `encoding`, but the README still warns the opposite in five places:

- L283 blockquote: "The `read` endpoint is **text-only** ... corrupts binary data"
- L290: "Then `GET /exec/<id>/read?path=shot.png.b64` and `base64 -d`"
- L303 troubleshooting row: "Screenshot file is not a PNG"
- L523 comment: "# Read a file from /workspace (text only — see below)"
- L540 blockquote: "`read` returns **text only**"

These were accurate when written (commit ad71c91) and became false when g9h.8 landed.
Delete them.

The browser walkthrough also teaches the obsolete workaround: its script does
`fs.writeFileSync("/workspace/shot.png.b64", shot.toString("base64"))` and reads the
`.b64` file back. Replace with `page.screenshot({ path: "/workspace/shot.png" })` and
`GET /exec/:id/read?path=shot.png&encoding=base64`, which is the whole point of g9h.8.

## 2. g9h.2 — build.env shipped, README still lists every variable by hand

templates/browser/build.env now supplies the sizing with `:=` defaults, so
`sudo ./templates/build.sh browser` is sufficient. The README still instructs a
seven-variable `sudo -E env ROOTFS_SIZE=2048 ... ./templates/build.sh browser`
invocation. Not wrong — an explicit value still wins — but it hides the mechanism and
will drift from build.env.

Replace with the short form, and document build.env: where it lives, that explicit
environment overrides it, and that the defaults are per template. Keep the existing note
about sudo hiding an nvm/fnm/volta node, which is still accurate.

## 3. g9h.1 — boot hooks shipped, the promised custom-templates note was not written

g9h.1's own description asks for a "README custom-templates note". The README's
"Building & Creating Custom Templates" section documents the read-only rootfs, ENV not
surviving `docker export`, and the absent device nodes, but says nothing about
/etc/sandbox/boot.d/*.sh.

Document: hooks live at /etc/sandbox/boot.d/*.sh, run after the pseudo-filesystems are
mounted and before READY is printed, and must not return until their daemons are
actually serving — the snapshot is taken at READY and would otherwise freeze a
half-started process into every restored VM.

## Sequencing

g9h.10 also rewrites parts of README for the desktop template. These two should not run
concurrently. A dependency has been added so this correction lands first; drop it if the
desktop documentation is the more urgent of the two.
close_reason: README reconciled: base64 read (walkthrough, warnings, troubleshooting), build.env short form + mechanism, boot.d hook note in custom templates

title: auth: shutdown flushes a stale key store over keys.json
description:
key-store.ts loads keys once per process and never re-reads. shutdown.ts calls
flushKeys() -> saveKeys(), which writes the in-memory array unconditionally.

A server that started with an empty store and is then stopped writes `[]` over
keys.json, destroying keys created by the CLI in the meantime. Observed directly:
created a key as root, stopped the server, keys.json was back to `[]` and the key was
rejected as "Invalid API key".

Compounding it, saveKeys swallows write errors into logger.warn, and LOG_LEVEL defaults
to "silent" (src/logger.ts:6 — the README claims "debug"). So `npm run keys create` run
as a non-root user against the root-owned /var/lib/agent-sandbox/ prints a success
banner with an API key that was never persisted.

Fix:
- track a `dirty` flag, set by createKey / touchKey / revokeKey / deleteKey / rotateKey
- flushKeys returns early when this process changed nothing, so a stale snapshot is
  never written over another process's work
- saveKeys returns boolean and clears the flag
- cli.ts `create` verifies the write landed and exits 1 with a clear message otherwise

Not fixed, and worth a separate issue: a running server still cannot see keys created
after it started, so key creation requires stopping the server.
